newsitem.title: INDIA: ITC dep. chairman placed in custody.
newsitem.headline: ITC dep. chairman placed in custody.

text.p: The deputy chairman of ITC Ltd, Saurabh Misra, and a senior executive arrested early on Friday for alleged foreign exchange violations were remanded in judicial custody by a local court, officials said.
The chief metropolitan magistrate rejected a bail plea by Misra and R. Ranganathan, chief executive officer of ITC's tobacco division, and ordered them into judicial custody until November 22.

Earlier, K.K. Kabirpanthi, deputy director of the eastern regional office of the Enforcement Directorate, said Misra and Ranganathan were charged with violating the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA).
"We have arrested the two on charges of serious Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) violation," Kabirpanthi told reporters.
The directorate arrested Misra and Ranganathan early on Friday, he said.
"It could be a frame-up," Saurabh Misra told reporters, when asked about his arrest.
Two former chairmen of ITC Ltd, K.L. Chugh and J.N. Sapru, were arrested last week and remanded in judicial custody until November 13 by a local court.

In London, British tobacco and financial services group B.A.T Industries Plc said on Wednesday its fundamental attitude to India and its associate company ITC Ltd remains positive and one of continued commitment.
B.A.T, which is the single biggest shareholder in ITC with 31.7 percent, has pledged to work with the company's other Indian institutional shareholders to monitor the situation.
"This is a very valuable investment... there is no change to our investment view of ITC," a B.A.T spokesman said.
Investigators quizzed Yogesh Deveshwar, ITC's chairman, for more than 18 hours on Monday and Tuesday in the investigations.
Last week, the Enforcement Directorate also arrested a director and three former officials for violation of foreign exchange rules.
